rule_level_problems.problem: Hb < 6 omitted from the urgent criteria; not representable (no unit) but nothing records this. Acceptable per brief.

check_for lists pregnancy/postpartum/shock/pallor/dizziness/asthenia/chest pain/assault, but omits the measurements the rule uses (systolic BP < 80, pulse >= 100, respiratory rate >= 30), so check list and priority rule disagree.

Footnote 1 defines shock as SBP<80, pulse>=100, RR>30 (strict), confusion/restlessness, weakness; shock is encoded as a bare finding with no criteria; RR > 30 vs >= 30 differs between box (>=30) and footnote (>30); rule follows box.

Flowchart section (non-urgent approach) has refer-within-2-weeks / next-day referrals (e.g. new bleeding >1 year after final period, bleeding easy bruising, mass in abdomen same week, TSH criteria with pulse >=100) that carry triage logic; no lower-priority evaluations encoded. Likely intended page scope is the red box only, but these are a miss against the house standard of priority evaluations.
No probable/possible diagnosis rules; page has 'treat for likely anaemia' (needs Hb, not representable) so none expected.

summary: The red-box urgent criteria are encoded faithfully (pregnancy, recent delivery/miscarriage/termination, shock/SBP<80, pallor with tachycardia/tachypnoea/dizziness/weakness/chest pain, sexual assault/rape) with correct structure; Hb<6 is correctly absent as not representable. Main problems are that check_for omits the measurement criteria the priority rule uses, and the non-urgent referral triage (outside the box, e.g. refer within 2 weeks, next day, same week) is not encoded at all.
